Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Google. **Send only**: Gladys posts
its messages and alerts in a Google Chat space through an **incoming webhook**.
Nothing is read back from Google Chat: you cannot talk to Gladys from there.

This integration has never been tested with a real Google Chat space: it is
written from Google's public documentation, and tested against simulated
answers.

## What you need

- A **Google Workspace Business or Enterprise** account with access to Google
  Chat. A free personal Google account (gmail.com) cannot create webhooks.
- Your Workspace administrator must allow users to add incoming webhooks
  (Admin console → Apps → Google Workspace → Google Chat → Chat apps).
- A space where the webhook is added (a webhook posts in its own space only).

## Create the webhook

1. In Google Chat, open the space, click its name → **Apps & integrations** →
   **Webhooks** → **Add webhook**.
2. Give it a name (e.g. "Gladys") and an avatar if you like, save.
3. Copy the URL. It looks like
   `https://chat.googleapis.com/v1/spaces/…/messages?key=…&token=…`.

**The URL is a secret**: anyone holding it can post in the space. Gladys keeps
it in its database, never shows it again and sends it only to Google Chat; the
integration never writes it in its logs, its status or its `/data` folder
(logs name a space by a short fingerprint, like `space #3fa91c`). If it leaks,
delete the webhook in the space and create a new one.

## Configuration

**Configuration** screen (administrator):

- **Default space: webhook URL** (optional): the space of the "Post in Google
  Chat" scene action and of the **Test** button.
- **Messages per hour, at most** (default 60, 1 to 600): all spaces together,
  the Test button included. Beyond it a message is **not sent** (the refusal is
  logged), it is never kept for later.

**My account** block (each user, administrators or not): paste the webhook URL
of the space where you want the messages Gladys sends **you** (scene action
"Send a message", system messages such as a failed backup or a low battery,
the answers of the assistant to a message you typed in Gladys). Clear it to
stop.

## The scene action "Post in Google Chat"

Posts a text in the default space. Optional **thread key**: messages with the
same key are grouped in one thread (letters, digits and `. _ : -`, 64 at
most). Outputs for the next actions: `posted`, `deduplicated` and
`message_name` (the name Google gives the message). When the same text (and
thread key) was sent to that space less than 15 s earlier and posted, nothing
is posted again: `posted` stays true (the message is in the space) and
`deduplicated` is true, so a fallback branch on `posted` does not fire.

The scene action waits for Google's answer: if the message is refused, or if
Google does not answer, the action fails and the scene goes on.

## What is sent, and when

- Nothing is sent without a Gladys message, a scene or a click on **Test**.
  No polling, no background traffic.
- Gladys writes Markdown; it is turned into the Google Chat syntax: bold,
  italic, strikethrough, code, links `[text](https://…)`, titles become a bold
  line. Texts longer than 4,096 characters are cut (ending with "…"), never
  inside a link or a code block. A mention typed in a text, code included (`<users/all>`),
  becomes plain `@all`: it never notifies the whole space.
- **Images are not sent** (a camera snapshot attached to a message): an
  incoming webhook posts text only. The text of the message is still posted.
- A "space" here is the **Google space** (the `spaces/…` part of the URL),
  shared by all its webhooks: two users with two webhooks of one space share
  its limits.
- **One message every 1.1 s per space** (Google's limit is one a second): a
  message waits its turn for up to about 2 s; a burst beyond that is not sent
  ("too many messages at once").
- **The same text to the same space within 15 s is posted once**: when several
  users receive the same space, a message Gladys sends to all of them appears
  once. A duplicate gets the outcome of the first message: if the first one
  failed, the duplicate fails too; it is never said "posted" before the first
  one is.

## Never sent twice

A message that may have reached Google is **never sent again**, so the integration
never posts it twice. What each answer leads to:

| Answer of Google Chat                          | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Posted (200)                                   | Done.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 429 (too many requests)                        | Nothing posted. The Google space (all its webhooks) is paused (the delay Google gives, else 1 min, then 2, 4… up to 6 h). During the pause, messages to that space are not sent. The pause survives a restart.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 401, 403, 404                                  | The URL is **refused**: webhook deleted, token revoked, or webhooks turned off by the administrator. Nothing more is sent to that URL until a new URL is saved, the **Test** button succeeds (default space), or **Forget the refused webhook URLs** is clicked. Kept across restarts as an 8-bit salted fingerprint, never the URL. Other webhooks of the same space are not refused. |
| Another 4xx                                    | Nothing posted (the message was rejected); the next message is tried.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 5xx                                            | Maybe posted, maybe not: **not sent again**, the space paused like a 429.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| No answer within 10 s                          | Maybe posted: not sent again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Network, DNS, certificate error before sending | Nothing sent; the next message is tried.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Gladys gives a message 5 seconds: the integration answers it within 3.5 s;
a message still waiting for Google then goes on and its outcome is logged.

## Test button

**Test the default space** posts one test message in the default space and
says what Google answered. It counts in the hourly cap and is not sent during a
pause, like any message; a click tries the default URL again even when it was
refused. Two clicks within 15 s: the second says "Already posted".

**Forget the refused webhook URLs** (administrator) clears every refusal: the
next message to each refused URL, of the default space or of a user, is tried
once. The click sends nothing. A user can also save a new URL in "My account".

## Status

The Configuration screen shows: ready (with or without a default space), a
default URL that is not a Google Chat webhook URL, a default URL refused by
Google, a pause in progress, or a configuration that could not be read (read
again every 5 s, then less and less often, up to every 5 min).

## Privacy

What leaves Gladys: the text of the messages, to Google Chat
(`chat.googleapis.com`) only, over HTTPS. A redirect is never followed. What
`/data/state.json` keeps: a random salt, 8-bit salted fingerprints of the
refused URLs and of the paused spaces (one URL in 256 shares a fingerprint, so
the file never confirms a URL), the end dates of the pauses and the times of the
messages of the last hour (for the hourly cap). Never a URL, a key, a token or
a message text.

A collision is possible: after a restart, the first message to a URL whose
fingerprint is the one of a refused URL is held back, with a message saying
it may be another URL. A default URL saved after the restart never inherits
such a mark. A user whose contact URL is held back this way asks the
administrator to click **Forget the refused webhook URLs** (or saves a new
URL); for the default space, the Test button also lifts it.

If `/data` cannot be read when the integration starts, messages still go; the
refusals, pauses and messages learnt since the start are kept in memory, but
those kept from before the restart are unknown until `/data` is read again
(every 10 s).

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Google Chat te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google Chat in Gladys | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Google. Send only: Gladys posts in a Google Chat space, nothing is read back. Incoming webhooks need a Google Workspace Business or Enterprise account, and the Workspace administrator must allow users to add webhooks; a free personal Google account cannot create one. In the space: name of the space → Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then copy its URL. Each Gladys user pastes the URL of their space in “My account” to receive the messages Gladys sends them; the default space below serves the “Post in Google Chat” scene action and the Test button. Nothing is ever sent without a Gladys message, a scene or a click. |
| Default space: webhook URL (optional) | `secret` | No | Used by the scene action and the Test button. The URL lets anyone post in the space: kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Google Chat, never written in the logs. |
| Messages per hour, at most | `number` | No | All spaces together, the Test button included. Beyond it, a message is not sent (it is logged). Google Chat itself takes one message a second per space. |

## Cómo instalar Google Chat en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Google Chat aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-google-chat:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-google-chat](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-google-chat).

Google Chat requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Google Chat es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
